title: Finance & Legal Operational Guidance: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, RevRec and Billing
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This guidance consolidates Redwood Inference's operational policies for annual budgeting and forecasting, contracts and legal lifecycle, procurement procedures, and revenue recognition (RevRec) / billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and engineering/product stakeholders who participate in planning, vendor engagements, and customer billing.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a single operational reference that ensures consistent decision-making, controls, and handoffs across budgeting, contracting, procurement, and revenue recognition.
- Scope: Applies to all business units and subsidiaries of Redwood Inference. Excludes personnel compensation policies (people-ops maintains those). Covers both cash and GAAP-aligned accounting treatments for RevRec.

1) Roles and ownership
- Finance (owner): overall budgeting cadence, forecast consolidation, RevRec accounting, monthly close, and control owners for billing and invoicing.
- Legal (owner): contract templates, clause approvals, signature authority advices, and managing legal risk for commercial agreements.
- Procurement (owner): vendor onboarding, purchase order (PO) issuance, and contract management system stewardship.
- Requesting team (owner): provides business justification, budget codes, and acceptance of delivered goods/services.
- Approvers: see approval matrix below.

2) Annual budgeting & rolling forecasting
Overview:
- Annual budget cycles run on a fiscal year basis (FY starting Jan 1). High-level calendar:
  1. June-August: strategic planning and top-down guidance issued by finance.
  2. September-October: business unit bottoms-up submissions.
  3. November: consolidation, scenario modeling, executive review.
  4. December: board submission and budget lock.
  5. Ongoing: monthly rolling forecast (12-month horizon) updated by the 7th business day each month.
Required artifacts:
- Budget template (P&L by function, capex schedule, headcount plan).
- Forecast pack (variance commentary, key assumptions, runway analysis for cash).
Thresholds and controls:
- Material variance threshold: +/- 5% YOY or plan; variances beyond this require annotated commentary and remediation plan.
- Forecast accuracy target: median absolute percentage error (MAPE) < 6% for revenue line items across rolling 12 months.
Assumptions and scenario planning:
- Include explicit assumptions for growth rates, churn, pricing changes, model hosting cost inflation, and committed capacity expenses.
- Maintain three scenarios: Base, Upside (+10-20% revenue), Downside (-10-25% revenue).

3) Contracts & legal process
Standard contract lifecycle steps:
1. Need articulation: Requesting team fills Contract Intake Form in Contract Management System (CMS) with business justification, budget code, commercial terms desired, and risk flags.
2. Template selection: Legal provides a standard template (MSA, SOW, SaaS agreement). Deviations must be flagged with redline rationale.
3. Legal review: Legal reviews for risk, export controls, data residency, indemnities, IP, and insurance.
4. Pricing and commercial review: Finance verifies revenue/expense recognition implications and billing cadence.
5. Approval & signature: follow approval matrix below.
6. Execution & repository: executed agreement uploaded to the CMS; contracts must be tagged with revenue impact, vendor/customer, renewal dates, and responsible owner.
7. Post-signature: Finance and Sales/CS add to billing schedule; procurement initiates vendor onboarding where applicable.
Approval matrix (commercial and procurement thresholds):
- Up to $10k (one-time or annual): Requesting manager approval.
- $10k-$100k: Department head + Finance review.
- $100k-$500k: Department head + Finance Director + Legal (if commercial terms deviate).
- > $500k or multi-year commitments > 24 months: CFO + General Counsel approval required.
- Any contract with material data residency, export controls, or customer-required indemnities: General Counsel sign-off mandatory regardless of dollar value.
Signature authority:
- Electronic signatures via approved e-sign platform (DocuSign) are valid when executed by authorized signatories listed in the Delegation of Authority registry.
Contract templates and standard clauses:
- Legal maintains canonical MSA, SaaS Agreement, Data Processing Addendum (DPA), SOW, and Reseller Agreement templates in CMS. Deviations must be annotated and approved.

4) Procurement procedures (vendor lifecycle)
Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Vendor profile in vendor master (corporate legal name, tax ID, payment terms, banking details).
- W-8/W-9 collected where applicable.
- Insurance certificate (if required by contract).
- Security questionnaire complete for vendors touching customer data; higher-risk vendors require security review by InfoSec.
Purchase request and PO process:
1. Requestor submits Purchase Request (PR) with business justification, budget code, and estimated spend.
2. Procurement validates vendor and issues purchase order (PO) for approved PRs. POs required for goods/services > $5k.
3. Receiving team confirms delivery/acceptance; finance matches PO, invoice, and receiving report before payment (3-way match).
Preferred vendor sourcing and competitive bids:
- For purchases > $50k, procurement must obtain at least 3 competitive bids unless waiver provided and documented.
Payment terms and vendor payment policy:
- Standard vendor payment terms: Net 30. Early payment discounts should be evaluated vs. cash position and approved by Finance Director.
Procurement KPIs:
- PO cycle time target: < 5 business days from PR approval to PO issuance.
- Vendor onboarding time: < 10 business days for standard vendors, subject to security review timelines.

5) Revenue recognition and billing policies (summary for product and services)
Principles (GAAP-compliant):
- Revenue is recognized when performance obligations in a contract with a customer are satisfied, measured at the transaction price, and allocated to each obligation.
- Recurring SaaS: recognized ratably over the service period once customer has access and control.
- One-time professional services: recognized upon completion of deliverables or over time if criteria for over-time recognition are met (contract specific).
Contract modifications and variable consideration:
- Contract modifications that add distinct goods/services are treated as separate contracts if priced commensurate with standalone selling prices. Otherwise, reallocate transaction price across remaining performance obligations.
- Variable consideration (discounts, credits, refunds) is estimated using expected value or most likely amount and constrained if highly uncertain.
Billing cadence and invoice rules:
- Standard billing cadence: monthly in arrears for usage-billed hosted API; monthly or annual invoicing for committed Dedicated/Private contracts per SOW.
- Invoices must include: contract reference, billing period, quantity/units, unit price, total, tax breakdown, payment instructions, and remittance details.
- Late invoice disputes: customer must raise within 45 days of invoice date; undisputed portion remains payable under terms.
Deferred revenue and cutoffs:
- Cash received for services not yet delivered is recorded as deferred revenue. Monthly close includes a revenue cut-off checklist maintained by Finance to ensure correct period recognition.
Collections and bad debt allowance:
- Collections owned by Finance with Sales escalation for customer disputes.
- Bad debt provision reviewed quarterly and aged receivables reported to the CFO. Policy: allowance target = 0.5% - 2% of AR depending on customer profile and delinquency.

6) Systems, tagging, and chart-of-accounts (CoA) guidance
- All POs, contracts, and PRs must include a valid budget code mapped to CoA. Finance provides a lookup table for product, cost center, and project codes.
- Contract tagging standard: [customer/vendor] - [contract-type] - [startYYYYMMDD] - [contract-owner]. Example: acme-corp_msa_20250101_salesops.
- Primary systems: ERP (NetSuite), Contract Management System (DocuSign + CMS), Procurement tool (Coupa), Billing system (Stripe + Zuora connector), and internal Finance data warehouse (Snowflake).

7) Reporting, KPIs and controls
Key reports produced monthly:
- Revenue waterfall (deferred -> recognized) by contract group.
- AR aging and DSO trend.
- Budget vs. actual P&L with variance commentary.
- Forecast accuracy dashboard.
KPIs targets:
- DSO target: < 45 days for self-serve customers; < 60 days for enterprise with negotiated terms.
- Forecast accuracy (revenue MAPE): < 6% (see above).
Controls:
- Segregation of duties between requestors/approvers, procurement, and payment execution.
- Mandatory 3-way match for PO-based payments.
- Quarterly internal audit of contracts and revenue streams by Finance + Internal Audit.

8) Audit, compliance, and record retention
- Contracts and financial records retained for minimum 7 years (legal may require longer for certain jurisdictions).
- Finance will produce supporting workpapers for external auditors quarterly and at year-end, including recognized revenue by contract and supporting billing schedules.
- Periodic reviews of revenue recognition policies for new product lines or go-to-market changes; legal and finance must approve material policy changes.

9) Escalation paths and exceptions
- Exceptions to thresholds require documented business case, Finance Director approval, and Legal sign-off for term deviations.
- Escalation: Requesting manager -> Department head -> Finance Director -> CFO/GC.

Appendix A — Example CoA mappings (sample rows):
- Revenue: 4000 - Hosted API Revenue
- Revenue: 4001 - Dedicated Capacity Revenue
- Revenue: 4002 - Private Deployment Licensing
- COGS: 5000 - Cloud GPU compute
- COGS: 5001 - Model licensing fees
- OpEx: 6000 - R&D salaries
- OpEx: 6100 - Sales & Marketing

Appendix B — Quick checklists
- Contract intake checklist: business justification, budget code, requested template, term lengths, renewal options, termination clauses, export control flags.
- Vendor onboarding quick checklist: W-9/W-8, bank details, insurance, security questionnaire, PO requirement confirmation.
- Billing pre-close checklist: invoices issued, deferred revenue rollforward, recognized revenue support, AR sub-ledger reconciliation.
